part_title: Encrypted S3 Access and Secrets Rotation

scenes.title: Cross-account encrypted S3 reads
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains cross-account encrypted s3 reads by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Account A owns the S3 bucket and a customer managed KMS key. Follow the upper gate: a reader role in Account B needs an IAM GetObject permission and Account A must authorize the cross-account principal through its bucket policy. Follow the lower gate: the owner's KMS key policy and the caller's IAM permissions must allow the required Decrypt operation. Both checks are independent. An explicit Deny at either gate blocks the request.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
S3 access and KMS key access must both succeed; diagnose their separate access errors.

scenes.title: Secrets Manager rotation workflow
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains secrets manager rotation workflow by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Start at the central Secrets Manager version labels. Step one creates an AWSPENDING credential while AWSCURRENT still identifies the active credential. The rotation Lambda or supported managed rotation then updates the target database or service. Step three tests whether the pending credential works. Step four promotes the successful version to AWSCURRENT; the old credential can remain available for a controlled fallback. Application clients and connection pools must also refresh.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Rotation needs target updates, testing, promotion and application refresh; it is not universal by default.

scenes.title: Parameter Store versus Secrets Manager
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains parameter store versus secrets manager by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

The central decision asks whether the value is configuration or a credential. The left panel shows Parameter Store with hierarchical names, such as slash prod slash api slash endpoint, and KMS-encrypted SecureString for suitable sensitive configuration. The right panel shows Secrets Manager for credentials with supported managed or Lambda rotation and optional cross-Region replication. A SecureString is encrypted, but encryption alone does not update the target service or rotate a password. Both services need scoped access.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Choose by value type and lifecycle, not simply by encryption capability.
